# Galaxy Layer Deferred Initialization - Session Summary

**Date:** November 15, 2025
**Branch:** `feature/galaxy-visual-integration`
**Status:** ✅ FIXED

---

## Issue

User reported: "Somehow the 'Default galaxy' is back. system needs to wait for user generation"

**Problem:** Galaxy particles were appearing on app load even though no galaxy had been generated by the user.

**Root Cause:** `ThreeSceneManager` constructor was calling `initializeGalaxyLayers()` immediately on app load, which created 3 `GalaxyParticleSystem` instances with particle data, even though they were set to `visible: false`.

---

## Solution

**Defer galaxy layer creation until first galaxy generation.**

### Changes Made

#### 1. `src/components/Canvas/ThreeSceneManager.tsx`

**Added initialization tracking flag (Line 58):**
```typescript
private galaxyLayersInitialized: boolean = false; // Track if layers have been created
```

**Removed constructor call (Lines 119-121):**
```typescript
// BEFORE:
// Initialize multi-layer galaxy system (Phase 2.5)
this.initializeGalaxyLayers();

// AFTER:
// Multi-layer galaxy system (Phase 2.5) - Deferred until first galaxy generation
// Galaxy layers will be created when user generates a galaxy, NOT on app load
// This ensures no default galaxy appears before user interaction
```

**Added conditional initialization in renderGalaxy() (Lines 880-888):**
```typescript
// Initialize galaxy layers on FIRST galaxy generation only
if (!this.galaxyLayersInitialized) {
  this.initializeGalaxyLayers();
  this.galaxyLayersInitialized = true;
  console.log('[ThreeSceneManager] Galaxy layers initialized on first generation');
}

// Visual layers are automatically updated via store subscription
// galaxy-store.initializeFromProceduralGalaxy() configures layers based on galaxy type
```

---

## User Flow (Updated)

### App Load
```
User opens app
  ↓
Scene renders with starfield only
  ↓
NO galaxy layers created
  ↓
NO particles exist in memory
  ↓
Clean initial state
```

### First Galaxy Generation
```
User enters seed → Clicks "Generate Galaxy"
  ↓
ThreeSceneManager.renderGalaxy() called
  ↓
Check: galaxyLayersInitialized === false
  ↓
Call initializeGalaxyLayers() (creates 3 GalaxyParticleSystem instances)
  ↓
Set galaxyLayersInitialized = true
  ↓
Subscribe to galaxy-store for reactive updates
  ↓
galaxy-store.initializeFromProceduralGalaxy() configures layers based on galaxy type
  ↓
Layer 1 becomes visible (Layers 2-3 hidden but configured)
  ↓
User sees single galaxy layer, can enable Layers 2-3 manually
```

### Subsequent Galaxy Generations
```
User generates new galaxy with different seed
  ↓
ThreeSceneManager.renderGalaxy() called
  ↓
Check: galaxyLayersInitialized === true
  ↓
Skip initialization (layers already exist)
  ↓
galaxy-store.initializeFromProceduralGalaxy() reconfigures existing layers
  ↓
Particles regenerated based on new galaxy type
  ↓
Layer 1 visible, Layers 2-3 hidden (reset to defaults)
```

## Technical Details

### Why Not Destroy Layers on Clear?

The current implementation keeps the 3 `GalaxyParticleSystem` instances alive when clearing the galaxy, only setting them to `invisible`. This is an optimization:

**Benefits:**
- Avoids repeated object creation/destruction
- Maintains store subscription
- Faster regeneration on subsequent galaxy creation

**Alternative (if memory is an issue):**
- Add a `destroyGalaxyLayers()` method
- Call from `clearGalaxy()` in system-store
- Recreate layers on next generation
- Tradeoff: slower regeneration, cleaner memory

### Store Subscription Lifecycle

The `galaxyStoreUnsubscribe` function is created once in `initializeGalaxyLayers()` and persists for the entire app lifecycle. This ensures:
- Real-time updates when user edits layers
- Reactive visibility toggles
- Live config changes (particle count, colors, etc.)

## Summary

The default galaxy visibility issue has been resolved by deferring the creation of galaxy particle systems until the user generates their first galaxy. This ensures:

✅ Clean app load with no galaxy visible
✅ Single layer visible on generation (user's request)
✅ Layers 2-3 available for manual enabling
✅ No wasted memory on unused particle systems

The system now correctly waits for user interaction before creating any galaxy visuals.
